item.title: What if an AI bubble bursts — and that accelerates AI job losses?
item.description: Research on past recessions suggests downturns can accelerate automation. That raises the specter of a double whammy for workers.

item.title: Why are some food prices up and others down? Here are the stories of 5 items
item.description: Here's what's behind the fluctuating costs of everyday grocery items such as ground beef, eggs and chocolate chip cookies.

item.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act
item.description: The warnings surfaced in a trove of unreported court records. "I have been fighting about fixing this for months with people who didn't think the harms are severe enough," wrote one executive.

item.title: Difficult times in agriculture are making it tough for the next generation of farmers
item.description: Many farmers across the U.S. are reaching retirement age. But lately, increasing volatility and sky-high prices in agriculture are making it tough for the next generation to take over.

item.title: Noah Adams, longtime host of NPR's All Things Considered, has died

item.title: What this bankruptcy says about AI startups
item.description: Character.AI collected millions of users, making it a very appealing acquisition. Google took a unique route to "acquiring" it, hiring away its founders and licensing its technology. Now Character.AI is filing for bankruptcy. Here's what to know.

item.title: Inside the race between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos for control of outer space
item.description: The Atlantic writer Josh Tyrangiel says Musk and Bezos each want to colonize the moon, mine its resources and launch thousands more satellites. He says their only real competition is each other.

item.description: Social Security benefits are set to get a boost to offset rising consumer prices. And, streamer Hasan Piker says the GOP's "guilt-by-association politics" won't drag Democrats down in the midterms.

item.title: Inflation sizzled in September — and Social Security benefits will get a boost
item.description: Consumer prices in September jumped 3.7% from a year ago. The Social Security Administration said benefits will increase next year to help keep pace with the rising cost of living.
